title: Attentional Blink
scopeNote: This keeps the performed rapid stream and the lag function it produces, which cannot be replaced by a description. The practice block with explanatory feedback on every stream, the second response mode and the across-block comparison stay in the longer version. The worked-example route is kept and moved to the front, because the paradigm cannot be slowed down without abolishing the effect and some learners should not run it at all.
summary: Letters arrive ten a second. Somewhere in each stream is a digit, and somewhere after it there may be an X. Reporting the digit costs a few hundred milliseconds in which the X is displayed, looked at, and not seen, and the learner's own accuracies draw that curve.
learningObjectives: Describe the rapid serial visual presentation paradigm and the role of the two targets.
Read a lag function and identify where accuracy for the second target falls and recovers.
Explain why accuracy for the second target is computed only over trials where the first was reported correctly.
Explain why catch trials with no second target are necessary.
Recognise that missing the second target is not a failure of vision or of effort.
interactionTypes: four slowed practice streams with the answers shown after each
a performed block of 31 streams at ten items a second, with results withheld
a lag function drawn from the learner's own accuracies
a fully labelled simulated route offered before the task for anyone who should not run it
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every response is scored in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: The rate of change is stated in a caution before the task rather than after it, along with the fact that the background never changes and nothing flashes or moves. Because rapid serial presentation cannot be slowed without abolishing the effect, a worked-example route is offered up front: it produces the same figure from simulated data, is labelled as simulated in the heading, the lead, the chart title, the chart description, the table caption and the notes, and reaches every conclusion the performed route reaches. Both responses are two-key, available from the keyboard or from labelled buttons, and neither is timed. The chart carries a description giving every value with its lag in milliseconds, and the table repeats them. Practice runs at less than half speed. Every stage is announced through a polite live region.
dataStatus: The learner's own accuracies on the performed route, or clearly labelled simulated data on the worked-example route. Nothing is a norm.
simulationNotes: Streams are 18 consonants with the first target, a digit, at position 5, 6 or 7, and the second target, an X, at lags of 1, 2, 3, 5 or 8 items, so 100 to 800 ms later. X is reserved for the second target and I, O and Q are excluded because they are confusable with digits at speed. Six streams contain no X at all, so reporting one is not free, and the false-alarm count is reported. The first target is reported as odd or even rather than by identity: two keys instead of six, the same requirement to have identified the digit, and a response fast enough not to eat into the next stream. Accuracy for the second target is computed only over streams where the first was reported correctly, which is not tidying but the definition: the blink is the cost of having processed the first target. The worked example uses the original's per-lag accuracy profile.
readmeTopic: the few hundred milliseconds after finding one target in which a second one is not seen
